name: Fat-soluble accumulation
aliases: Fat-soluble accumulation, lipophilic compound accumulation, bioaccumulation in fatty tissue, fat storage of toxins
what_is: The process by which lipophilic (fat-soluble) compounds accumulate in the body's fatty tissue over years. These compounds release during periods of rapid fat loss, pregnancy, breastfeeding, or menopause.
why_botia: BOTIA surfaces this risk because women naturally have a higher body fat percentage, making them more vulnerable to the accumulation of fat-soluble toxins. These compounds can release in concentrated form during key life stages, potentially affecting the woman and, during breastfeeding, the infant.
can_1: Provide contextual information on how fat-soluble compounds behave in the female body.
can_2: Connect this knowledge to specific ingredients flagged on the label when applicable.
cannot_1: Measure the actual burden of fat-soluble compounds in a specific person from the label.
cannot_2: Predict when or at what concentration accumulated compounds may release.
